title: AI Incident Reporting Act
last_action: Introduced and referred to House Energy and Commerce. No hearing or markup located by the cutoff.
summary: Requires covered high-risk model developers to report specified autonomy, cybersecurity, and model-weight-theft incidents within seven days. Commerce would receive investigative authority and civil-penalty authority reaching $2 million per violation.
committee_dynamics: The mandatory reporting and penalty structure gives Energy and Commerce a central role. Its definitions and seven-day clock overlap with, but differ from, FRONTIER and other vulnerability-reporting proposals.
advance_rationale: Limited coalition and no committee action make standalone passage difficult, although the reporting concepts are plausible amendment material.
verification_level: Primary-source verified in the September 1, 2026 research pass
